summary: Iteration 10 testing complete: MeteoAlarm primary vigilance source and trajectory spatial-clustering both validated end-to-end. Live MeteoAlarm endpoint returns 'Vigilance jaune orages' for all 7 target depts (65, 64, 32, 31, 09, 66, 40) — matching official vigilance.meteofrance.fr. Frontend VigilanceBanner displays yellow (#FFFBEB bg) with correct per-phenomenon colors and MeteoAlarm disclaimer. Trajectory clustering unit-tested with 6 scenarios (not_enough / stationary / noise / happy / no_dominant_cluster / signal_from_noise). All 64 backend tests pass (59 integration + 5 new trajectory units including 2 new clustering tests). All frontend critical selectors present and no JS errors.

minor.issue: analyze_approach NOT updated with spatial clustering like predict_trajectory — live response shows VITESSE=795 km/h, ETA=5 min on the 'Orage en approche' banner, which is the same dispersion-noise problem the trajectory endpoint now guards against. Consider applying _find_dominant_cluster (or equivalent) to analyze_approach or gating alerts on a plausibility check (speed<=120).

issues: 'ORAGE EN APPROCHE' banner still shows implausible speed (795 km/h) because /api/storms/approach isn't clustered — main agent may want to hide or clamp alerts when approach speed >120 km/h, mirroring predict_trajectory noise_too_high guard.

action_items: Consider applying the same spatial-clustering + speed-plausibility guard used in predict_trajectory to analyze_approach — live UI currently shows ETA '5 min / 795 km/h' which is the same noise problem the trajectory fix addresses.
critical_code_review_comments: vigilance.py: _fetch_meteoalarm correctly caches for 15 min via _cached helper (matches TTL comment in server.py _alert_watcher). NUTS3 mapping is correct (FR626=Hautes-Pyrénées verified via live MeteoAlarm feed). Language filter 'fr-FR' de-duplicates multi-language alert info blocks — good.
vigilance.py: _parse_awareness_level uses split(';') and clamps to 1-4 — safe. _parse_iso uses datetime.fromisoformat which is Python3.11+ only; /root/.venv is 3.11 so OK but flag if downgrade.

vigilance.py: Fallback chain (meteoalarm → open-meteo-fallback → raise) is defensive. _compute_from_openmeteo_fallback has a subtle bug: passes `_do` (coroutine fn) directly to `if callable(_do) else []` then awaits it — simplifies to always calling `_do()`; code works but logic is redundant. Minor.

analysis.py _find_dominant_cluster: 0.25° grid + 9-cell neighbourhood = ~83km box. Correctly rejects fully-dispersed 10-strike noise (test_no_dominant_cluster) AND extracts dominant signal from mixed noise (test_dominant_cluster_extracts_signal_from_noise). Good.

analysis.py predict_trajectory: speed_kmh>120 / <3 guards still fire AFTER clustering, which is correct belt-and-suspenders. Live app confirms: trajectory endpoint returns reason='noise_too_high' with ~18009 km/h in current storm activity — badge renders 'Dispersion trop élevée' correctly.

GAP: analyze_approach() in analysis.py still uses naive median-split strategy without clustering — its output currently drives the 'Orage en approche' red banner which shows VITESSE 795 KM/H. Same noise problem as trajectory had pre-iteration-10. Recommend applying _find_dominant_cluster or a plausibility clamp before displaying to users.
server.py /api/weather/vigilance unchanged signature, backward-compatible with VigilanceBanner.jsx (which consumes departements[].phenomena[] and overall_*). Good.
VigilanceBanner renders all 8 phenomena correctly (ORAGES, VENT VIOLENT, PLUIE-INONDATION, CANICULE, GRAND FROID, NEIGE-VERGLAS, BROUILLARD, AVALANCHES) when expanded — previous iteration only had 6.
Disclaimer text 'Vigilance officielle Météo-France agrégée par MeteoAlarm (EUMETNET)' visible in expanded view — user-facing attribution is correct.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_storm_tracker.py (updated TestVigilance: 7 depts instead of 5, 8 phenomena instead of 6, source='meteoalarm'|'open-meteo-fallback', added test_vigilance_meta_arrays, added source_label/source_url/updated_at assertions)

/app/backend/tests/test_trajectory_unit.py (added test_no_dominant_cluster and test_dominant_cluster_extracts_signal_from_noise; adjusted test_noise_too_high to reflect clustering-first behaviour; tightened happy-path strike spacing to fit a single 0.25° cell cluster)

context_for_next_testing_agent: ITER-10 VALIDATED: (1) /api/weather/vigilance now returns source='meteoalarm', source_label='Météo-France (via MeteoAlarm)', 7 depts (09/31/32/40/64/65/66) with NUTS3 codes, 8 phenomena per dept (orage/vent/pluie/canicule/grand-froid/neige/brouillard/avalanche). Live response shows all 7 depts at level=2 'jaune' for orage — matches official vigilance.meteofrance.fr. Fallback path returns source='open-meteo-fallback' (verified by code review). (2) predict_trajectory uses _find_dominant_cluster (0.25° grid + 9-cell neighbourhood, min_points=4) before linear regression. Rejection reasons: not_enough_strikes (<4), no_dominant_cluster (<4 in best cell), static_centroid, noise_too_high (>120 km/h), stationary (<3 km/h). Happy path detects coherent cluster moving at plausible speed. (3) Frontend VigilanceBanner (testid=vigilance-banner) renders yellow bg #FFFBEB when overall=jaune, expand button (testid=vigilance-toggle) shows 8 phenomena + 6 neighbouring depts + disclaimer. (4) KNOWN GAP: /api/storms/approach (analyze_approach) still naive — shows 795 km/h on live UI banner. Not part of this iteration's fix scope, flagged to main agent. (5) All regression selectors present: timeline-preset-0, toggle-clouds, toggle-rain, toggle-wind, toggle-trajectory, trajectory-badge. Test command: cd /app && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://storm-monitor-20km.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v
rca_of_the_issue: Previous iteration: vigilance mismatch between app (green) and Météo-France (jaune). RCA: app computed vigilance locally from Open-Meteo thresholds which lagged / diverged from official MF criteria. Mitigation (applied in this iteration): switched to MeteoAlarm feed (EUMETNET aggregator of official national services including MF). Verified live: all 7 target depts now show level 2 orage matching vigilance.meteofrance.fr. Open-Meteo is kept only as last-resort fallback.
